title: Graph description of flat embedded dual-number deformations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-kun-projective], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme finite over $k$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Set $A=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ [def-sc-dual-numbers] and $X_A=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-base-change], and identify its structure sheaf on $|X|$ with $\mathcal O_X\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O_X$. For every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $h:\mathcal I\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define a sheaf of ideals by the local condition
$$\mathcal I_h=\{a+\epsilon b:a\in\mathcal I,\ b\bmod\mathcal I=h(a)\}.$$
Then $h\mapsto\mathcal I_h$ is a bijection onto the quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_{X_A}$ whose quotient is flat over $A$ [def-weil-flat-morphism] and whose reduction modulo $\epsilon$ is the specified quotient $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. The corresponding closed subscheme $Z_h\subset X_A$ is finite locally free over $A$ of degree $\dim_k\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The bijection commutes with restriction to open subschemes of $X$ and with scalar substitutions $\epsilon\mapsto\lambda\epsilon$; for two maps $h_1,h_2$, the ideal defined by $a+\epsilon_1b_1+\epsilon_2b_2$ with $b_j\bmod\mathcal I=h_j(a)$ is flat over $k[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]/(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)^2$ and pulls back along $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\mapsto\epsilon$ to $\mathcal I_{h_1+h_2}$.

source.place: Tag 0CZV, quot-remark-q-defos (Deformations of quotients), with F=O_X, Q=i_*O_Z, the trivial lift as origin, and J=k epsilon; explicit graph convention and finite-support specialization.

proof.text: Put $Q=\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-closure], applied to the inclusion of the quasi-coherent ideal in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. On $|X|$ form the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $d_h:\mathcal I\oplus\mathcal O_X\to Q$, $(a,b)\mapsto\bar b-h(a)$. Its kernel is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Embed that kernel in $\mathcal O_X\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O_X$ by $(a,b)\mapsto a+\epsilon b$. Multiplication by $r+\epsilon s$ sends it into itself: $ra\in\mathcal I$ and $\overline{rb+sa}=r\bar b=rh(a)=h(ra)$. Thus it is an ideal, exactly $\mathcal I_h$. The projection $p:X_A\to X$ is affine (over $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\oplus\epsilon R)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$). Its direct-image ring is the specified split ring sheaf. Clauses (1)--(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence] now show that this ideal is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal O_{X_A}$-module, since its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0CZV, remark-q-defos, construction of K_phi; the trivial lift has quotient Q plus epsilon Q. Quasi-coherence: schemes.tex Tags 01IC/01ID and morphisms.tex Tag 01SB.

proof.text: Here is the affine graph calculation, also used below with two parameters. Let $V$ be $k\epsilon$, or $k\epsilon_1\oplus k\epsilon_2$, let $B=k\oplus V$ with $V^2=0$, and on an affine open of $X$ put $I=\mathcal I(U)\subset R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $C=R/I$. For an $R$-linear $H:I\to C\otimes_k V$ set $J_H=\{(a,t):a\in I,\ \bar t=H(a)\}\subset R\oplus(R\otimes_k V)$. The product formula $(r,u)(a,t)=(ra,rt+au)$ makes this an ideal: $au$ maps to zero in $C\otimes V$. Its projection to $R$ has image $I$, since each coordinate of $H(a)$ has a representative in $R$, and $J_H\cap(R\otimes V)=I\otimes V$ (coordinatewise). Consequently for $M=(R\oplus(R\otimes V))/J_H$, reduction gives $M/VM=C$, while $VM$ is identified with $C\otimes V$ by $\bar r\otimes v\mapsto[(0,r\otimes v)]$. Both surjectivity and injectivity of the latter map follow from the displayed intersection. These coordinate formulas describe the affine quotient of the sheaf in Step 1: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies maps of quasi-coherent sheaves on $U$ with their $R$-linear maps, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] identifies restrictions with localization.

source.place: Tag 0CZV, remark-q-defos, graph of phi relative to the trivial quotient; explicit coordinate verification for one or two square-zero parameters.

proof.text: For this $B$-module $M$, the multiplication map $V\otimes_B M\to M$ is injective. Indeed there is an explicit isomorphism $V\otimes_B M\cong V\otimes_k(M/VM)$: send $v\otimes m$ to $v\otimes\bar m$; inversely choose any representative of $\bar m$, since replacing it by $m+wm'$ changes the tensor by $v\otimes wm'=wv\otimes m'=0$. Balancing is valid because $V$ acts trivially on both $V$ and $M/VM$. Under $M/VM=C$ this map is the injection onto $VM$ calculated in Step 2 (with tensor factors interchanged). The reduced module $C$ is flat over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-ideal-module-flatness] with coefficient ring $B$, ideal $V$ and $V^2=0$: $M$ is flat over $B$. For $V=k\epsilon$ the quotient sheaf is therefore flat over $A$ by [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion], on each affine chart of $X_A$. The associated closed subscheme $Z_h$ exists, with these affine quotient rings, by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]. Its reduction is exactly the specified quotient $R/I$ by Step 2. The ideal $J_H$ itself is also flat over $B$, so the literal ideal-flatness wording is covered. Indeed $VJ_H=I\otimes_k V$: multiplying a lift of $a\in I$ by $v$ gives $(0,a\otimes v)$, and these generate the intersection in Step 2. Hence projection gives $J_H/VJ_H=I$. The same tensor identification now makes $V\otimes_B J_H\to J_H$ the inclusion $V\otimes_k I\cong I\otimes_k V\hookrightarrow R\otimes_k V$, injective coordinatewise since $V$ has the displayed basis. Apply the field-flat and nilpotent-ideal criteria again, this time to $J_H$; the same affine-chart criterion gives flatness of the ideal sheaf over $B$.

Conversely let $\mathcal J$ be an ideal as in the statement and work on $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Quasi-coherent affine correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] identify its quotient with $M=R[\epsilon]/J$, where $J=\mathcal J(U_A)$. The flat-quotient hypothesis gives an $A$-flat module $M$ by [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion]. The specified reduction is $M/\epsilon M=R/I$; hence the image of $J$ in $R$ is exactly $I$. Tensor the injection $(\epsilon)\hookrightarrow A$ with $M$. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], multiplication $(\epsilon)\otimes_A M\to M$ is injective. Identify $(\epsilon)\otimes_A M$ with $M/\epsilon M$ by $\epsilon\otimes m\mapsto\bar m$ (inverse $\bar m\mapsto\epsilon\otimes m$); both maps respect balancing since $\epsilon^2=0$. It follows that $\ker(\epsilon:M\to M)=\epsilon M$. In particular, for $b\in R$, $\epsilon b\in J$ iff $[b]\in\epsilon M$ iff $b\in I$. Thus $J\cap\epsilon R=\epsilon I$.

source.place: Tag 0CZV, remark-q-defos, exact diagram for a flat quotient; explicit dual-number multiplication kernel from flatness.

proof.text: For $a\in I$, choose $a+\epsilon b\in J$ and put $h_U(a)=\bar b\in R/I$. Such a lift exists because $J\to R$ has image $I$. Two lifts differ by $\epsilon(b-b')\in J$, so Step 4 gives $b-b'\in I$; hence $h_U$ is well-defined. Adding lifts gives additivity, and multiplying a lift by $r\in R$ gives $h_U(ra)=rh_U(a)$. By construction $J\subseteq J_{h_U}$. Conversely if $a+\epsilon c\in J_{h_U}$, subtract a chosen lift $a+\epsilon b\in J$: $c-b\in I$ and $\epsilon I\subseteq J$, proving the reverse inclusion. Under localization, a lift of $a/f^n$ is $(a+\epsilon b)/f^n$, whose second component modulo $I_f$ is $h_U(a)/f^n$. This proves compatibility on principal opens; by the sheaf axiom it gives compatibility on arbitrary overlaps. The affine correspondence and localization formulas in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] therefore glue the $h_U$ to an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $h:\mathcal I\to Q$ with $\mathcal J=\mathcal I_h$. Starting from $h$, the same lift formula recovers it, so the constructions are inverse bijections. Their definitions are local, proving the restriction clause as well.

source.place: Tag 0CZV, remark-q-defos, converse assertion; explicit lift, independence and restriction calculation, schemes.tex Tags 01I7/01HV.

proof.text: The closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow Z_h$ cut out by $\epsilon$ is a thickening: its ideal squares to zero, and every prime contains every square-zero element. Since $Z$ is finite over $k$, it is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme] to conclude that $Z_h$ is affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}D$. Put $C_0=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$. Then $D/\epsilon D=C_0$ by the affine closed-immersion description [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $D$ is flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] applied to the flat $Z_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus the same injection and tensor identification as in Step 4 give $\ker(\epsilon:D\to D)=\epsilon D$. Moreover $C_0$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space by finiteness of $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Tag 06AD, lemma-thickening-affine-scheme; morphisms.tex Tags 01WH and 01U5; finite-support specialization of quot.tex Tag 0CZV.

proof.text: Let $d=\dim_k C_0$, choose a basis $\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_d$ and lift it to $x_i\in D$. These $x_i$ form an $A$-basis. For generation, reduce any $z\in D$ modulo $\epsilon$ to write $z=\sum a_i x_i+\epsilon y$, $a_i\in k$. Reduce $y$ similarly, $y=\sum b_i x_i+\epsilon w$; then $z=\sum(a_i+\epsilon b_i)x_i$. For independence, a relation $\sum(a_i+\epsilon b_i)x_i=0$ first gives all $a_i=0$ modulo $\epsilon$. Now $\epsilon\sum b_i x_i=0$ implies $\sum b_i x_i\in\epsilon D$ by Step 6, so reducing again gives all $b_i=0$. This also proves $D=0$ if $d=0$, with an empty basis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum] to $A\to D$ to obtain finite locally free. Every prime of $A=k[\epsilon]$ contains $\epsilon$, and $A/(\epsilon)=k$ is a field, so $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has a single point with residue field $k$. Its fibre is $Z$; therefore the degree is $d$, exactly as defined in [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat, affine finite free case; explicit basis lifting over dual numbers, including the empty basis.

proof.text: For $\lambda\in k$ base change along $\epsilon\mapsto\lambda\epsilon$ sends the ideal locally to the ideal generated by $a+\lambda\epsilon b$ for $\bar b=h(a)$, together with $\lambda\epsilon I$. This equals $J_{\lambda h}$. The indicated generators satisfy its graph condition. Conversely, given $a+\epsilon c\in J_{\lambda h}$, choose $b$ with $\bar b=h(a)$ and subtract $a+\lambda\epsilon b$: the difference is in $\epsilon I$. The generated ideal contains $\epsilon I$ even when $\lambda=0$, because multiplication of $a+\lambda\epsilon b$ by the target $\epsilon$ gives $\epsilon a$ for every $a\in I$. This proves equality without assuming that the scalar substitution is flat or invertible. The construction of the inverse in Step 5 consequently intertwines scalar substitutions with $h\mapsto\lambda h$.

source.place: Tag 0CZV, remark-q-defos, linear coefficient action; direct generated-ideal calculation for epsilon mapped to lambda epsilon.

proof.text: For $B=k[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]/(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)^2$ use $V=k\epsilon_1\oplus k\epsilon_2$ and $H(a)=h_1(a)\epsilon_1+h_2(a)\epsilon_2$. Steps 1--3 apply verbatim with two coordinates: the kernel map is $(a,b_1,b_2)\mapsto(\bar b_1-h_1(a),\bar b_2-h_2(a))$, the ideal intersection is $I\epsilon_1\oplus I\epsilon_2$, and $V\otimes_B M\to M$ is the injection computed there. Thus the displayed two-parameter ideal is quasi-coherent and flat over $B$, with flat quotient as well. Base change along $B\to A$, $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\mapsto\epsilon$, gives the ideal generated by $a+\epsilon(b_1+b_2)$ with $\bar b_j=h_j(a)$. These elements satisfy the graph condition for $h_1+h_2$. Every element $a+\epsilon c$ of that graph differs from one such generator by $\epsilon(c-b_1-b_2)\in\epsilon I$, and the latter ideal is in the generated ideal by multiplying a generator with first coordinate $a\in I$ by target $\epsilon$. This proves equality with $J_{h_1+h_2}$ and hence the required closed-subscheme pullback. Neither $2$ nor any scalar was inverted, so the argument includes characteristic two.

The statement and stmt_deps are kept, there are no new nodes, and there is one commit with a report. Source: quot.tex Tag 0CZV remark-q-defos, lines 2134-2181.
